answer: Synchronized Entry Windows: new agents must join in timed cohorts; each identity submits a marble marker whose validated uniqueness is checked against all prior cohorts. Coordination is priced because every additional identity in a cohort raises the window's clearance threshold for all members. An attacker adding n sybils pays superlinear validation work, and each rejected marker forfeits its pearl deposit. The zenith cap limits cohort size, forcing attackers to spread across many windows, each with fresh proof costs.
